recently_updated.summary: New question QB1_K Q8 added from an August 2026 Kochi MMD candidate report (Vivek, via Nixon, WhatsApp): Simon asked 'what is CSR?', meaning the IACS Common Structural Rules. The candidate's submitted scope statement (bulk carriers 90 m+, double-hull oil tankers 150 m+) was verified correct but incomplete — it omitted the construction-contract applicability, without which the scope is unanswerable against the standard examiner follow-up ('my 200 m bulker was built 2003 — was it CSR?'). Verified against primary sources: original separate CSR-BC/CSR-OT adopted by IACS Council December 2005, applicable to ships contracted for construction on or after 1 April 2006 (confirmed from the CSR for Bulk Carriers January 2006 rule text application clause, and ClassNK's CSR page); harmonised CSR BC & OT in force 1 July 2015, applicable to contracts dated on or after 1 July 2015 (ClassNK). Rules point to IACS PR No. 29 for the meaning of 'contracted for construction'. Second verified correction, and the core teaching point of the card: CSR scope is NOT identical to SOLAS II-1 Reg. 3-10 (GBS) scope. GBS applies at 150 m and above for BOTH ship types (Res. MSC.290(87), in force 1 Jan 2012; contract 1 Jul 2016 / keel 1 Jul 2017 / delivery 1 Jul 2020), and excludes ore carriers and combination carriers — so a 120 m bulk carrier can be a CSR ship but not a Reg. 3-10 ship. Also corrected the 'why is CSR mandatory' explanation away from both 'IACS made it mandatory' and 'SOLAS makes CSR mandatory' to the accurate four-step chain (class rules → flag/RO, statutory and commercial framework → Reg. 3-10 requires conforming RO/Administration structural rules → IACS CSR verified through the IMO GBS process, MSC 96 confirming the 12 IACS Members' rules conform). IACS's claim that CSR are the only Rules complying with GBS is retained but explicitly attributed to IACS, not presented as a SOLAS requirement. Added the five-tier GBS framework (MSC.287(87) / MSC.1/Circ.1394/Rev.2) and a Ship Construction File section built from the actual text of MSC.1/Circ.1343 (2 June 2010) — four content groups (Design, Construction, In-service, Recycling), storage on board vs shore archive, and the update-on-major-event rule. Time-sensitive 'CSR review underway' material deliberately quarantined in a separate 'Current status — not exam-essential' deep-dive so it cannot age into the memorisation body. Cheat sheet updated with a Q8 flip card, two new confusable-pair boxes (CSR-vs-GBS scope; Common Structural Rules vs Continuous Synopsis Record vs CSM), and a rapid-recall row. Related repo sweep run the same session for stale IMO Net-Zero Framework adoption claims and pre-Omnibus CSRD thresholds: 27 NZF assertion-shaped hits across 22 files all confirmed to be negation-context warnings against the error (no corrections needed); zero CSRD mentions repo-wide. HTML tag balance clean, all 4 script blocks pass node --check, auth gate intact.

recently_updated.note: PSC appeal-chain correction cascade, triggered by a subscriber correction report (Rathesh) on QB4_E Q8. Root cause: the appeal escalation chain's Stage 3 review deadline was stated platform-wide as '120 days from the ship's release from detention' and implicitly presented as flowing from IMO Resolution A.1206(34) itself.
